requirement:
# REQ-2283: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2283

#### Bug description

Both `MessagePackGenerator` (CS8785) and `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer` (AD0001) throw `IndexOutOfRangeException` when a `[MessagePackObject]` type has a member whose type is a **closed generic value type defined in a referenced assembly**.

Because the generator then "will not contribute to the output", the compiling assembly silently ends up with **no generated resolver at all**. It is only a warning, so a normal build looks fine, but trimmed and NativeAOT apps fail at runtime. In our case three assemblies of a large app had been shipping without a resolver across two releases before we noticed.

#### Repro steps

Two projects. `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack;
namespace Lib;

[MessagePackObject]
public partial record struct Item<T>([property: Key(0)] string Key);
```

`app`, with a `ProjectReference` to `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack; using Lib;
namespace App;

[MessagePackObject]
public sealed partial record Cmd([property: Key(0)] string Scope)
{
    [Key(1)] public Item<int> Member { get; init; }
}
```

Then `dotnet build` on `app`. Both projects are in the attached `mp-repro.zip`.

#### Expected behavior

A clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.
#### Actual behavior

```
CSC : warning CS8785: Generator 'MessagePackGenerator' failed to generate source. It will not
contribute to the output and compilation errors may occur as a result. Exception was of type
'IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the bounds of the array.'.
CSC : warning AD0001: Analyzer 'MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Analyzers.MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer'
threw an exception of type 'System.IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the
bounds of the array.'.
```

`app.dll` contains no `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`.

- Version used: MessagePack 3.1.8
- Runtime: .NET 10 (SDK 10.0.204), Windows 11

#### Additional context

**What triggers it.** `Item` is declared in `lib`, `Cmd` in `app`:

| `Item` declared as | result |
|---|---|
| `record struct Item<T>` | **crash** |
| `struct Item<T>` | **crash** |
| `struct Item` | ok |
| `record struct Item` | ok |
| `class Item<T>` | ok |
| `record class Item<T>` | ok |

So it needs all three of: **generic**, **value type**, **from a referenced assembly**. Moving the identical `Item<T>` declaration into `app` itself makes the crash disappear, which is what makes this specific to metadata symbols.
**Stack trace.**

```
System.IndexOutOfRangeException: Index was outside the bounds of the array.
   at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo(INamedTypeSymbol formattedType, ISymbol callerSymbol)
   at TypeCollector.CollectGeneric(INamedTypeSymbol type, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 661
   at TypeCollector.CollectCore(ITypeSymbol typeSymbol, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 371
   at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo(INamedTypeSymbol formattedType, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 1062
   at TypeCollector.CollectCore(ITypeSymbol typeSymbol, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 386
   at TypeCollector.Collect() in TypeCollector.cs:line 300
   at MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.AnalyzeSymbol(SymbolAnalysisContext, ReferenceSymbols, AnalyzerOptions) in MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.cs:line 431
```

`CollectGeneric` line 661 is the closed-generic branch that calls `GetObjectInfo` directly:

```csharp
else
{
    // NOTE: ... closed generic types such as `Foo<string>` are not registered as a formatter.
    this.GetObjectInfo(type, callerSymbol);
```

so `GetObjectInfo` runs against a type that has no syntax. Several diagnostic paths inside it index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly (lines 735, 1009, 1101) instead of using `FirstOrDefault()` the way the neighbouring `GetIdentifierLocation` / `GetLocation` / `GetParameterListLocation` helpers already do, and that collection is empty for a metadata symbol. I did not narrow down which of the three fires.

**Getting the stack trace.** Console output truncates the exception to its message; `-p:ErrorLog=out.sarif` preserves the full description, including the stack trace and an `ISymbol:` context line naming the offending type:

```
dotnet build -p:ErrorLog=out.sarif
```

**Workaround.** Putting `[MessagePackFormatter(typeof(ItemFormatter<>))]` on the generic value type short-circuits `CollectCore` (line 356) before `GetObjectInfo` is reached, at the cost of hand-writing the formatter.

**Possibly related:** #2092 reports CS8785 from the v3 generator, but with a different inner exception and no repro.

story.summary: Stops the source generator and the MsgPack00x analyzer from crashing when a [MessagePackObject] member's type is a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly. It does this in three ways. First, every diagnostic the TypeCollector reports now goes through a new filter that drops any diagnostic whose location is not source in the current compilation. Second, two sites that indexed `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` now tolerate a symbol with no syntax. Third, three new tests compile a defining assembly to a metadata-only image and check that the consuming project builds with no diagnostics and gets a resolver.
story.why: For metadata symbols `DeclaringSyntaxReferences` is empty, so indexing `[0]` threw IndexOutOfRangeException. The generator then produced no resolver at all, which breaks trimmed and NativeAOT apps.
touches_beyond_requirement: The new diagnostic filter (TypeCollector.cs 239, 1436-1450) applies to every diagnostic the TypeCollector reports, not only those about metadata types. Any diagnostic created with a null or Location.None location is now silently dropped.
README.md gains a new section, and doc/analyzers/MsgPack004.md documents a new policy: problems in referenced types are only reported by the defining project.
story.confidence_overview: High that the reported repro (a record struct with keyed members) no longer crashes; the record-struct test mirrors the issue. Medium that all crash sites are covered. The issue names three `[0]` sites (old lines 735, 1009, 1101), but only two visibly change here. Low test coverage for the BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull path. The broad filter is a behaviour change the owner should decide on.

In addition, no test covers this path.

claims.text: The collector's reportDiagnostic delegate is wrapped so a diagnostic is forwarded only when its Location.IsInSource is true and its SourceTree belongs to the compilation being analyzed; all other diagnostics are dropped.

Second, it runs the MessagePackGenerator directly via CSharpGeneratorDriver and asserts there is no warning-or-higher generator diagnostic (which would include CS8785) and that the expected resolver hint name is produced.

breaker.reason: Checked GenericsFormatterTests.cs lines 628-659: RunWithMetadataReferenceAsync first runs VerifyCS.Test with definingAssembly in AdditionalReferences and no expected diagnostics, then runs MessagePackGenerator directly via CSharpGeneratorDriver, asserting no warning-or-higher diagnostics (which covers CS8785 emitted by GeneratorDriver on generator exceptions) and asserting expectedResolverHintName is present in GeneratedSources.

claims.text: The helpers CompileToMetadataReferenceAsync and CreateCompilation emit the defining source to an in-memory image and return MetadataReference.CreateFromImage. The referenced type therefore truly has no syntax references, matching the metadata-symbol trigger. They throw if the defining compile fails.

findings.description: Claim C2 disputed: TypeCollector.cs line 1434 also changes the hard cast (PropertyDeclarationSyntax) from line 985 to a safe cast (as PropertyDeclarationSyntax), which the claim omits, and contradicts its cited XML doc at lines 1430-1433: GetPropertyIdentifierLocation returns null not only for metadata properties with no source declaration, but also for source-declared positional record and record-struct properties whose syntax node is ParameterSyntax (e.g., [property: Key(null!)] string Key), causing ReportIfLocatedInCompilation at line 1446 to silently drop BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull even in the defining project. In addition, no test covers this path.

Claim C5 disputed: GenericsFormatterTests.cs lines 562-577 do not reproduce the issue's App code verbatim: lines 575-576 add an explicit [GeneratedMessagePackResolver] partial class AppResolver { }, whereas the issue's App snippet has no custom resolver class and relies on the default auto-generated GeneratedMessagePackResolver (and CompileToMetadataReferenceAsync at line 635 compiles Lib without running MessagePackGenerator, unlike the issue's ProjectReference).

The issue lists three `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` sites (old lines 735, 1009, 1101). Only two are visibly changed, at new lines 985 and 1077. If a third direct `[0]` index (around the old line 735 region) remains outside the diff, other metadata-type shapes could still crash. Verify that no `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` remains in TypeCollector.cs.

The filter drops every diagnostic whose location is not in source, not just those for metadata types. A diagnostic about a source type that is created with a null location is now silently suppressed, where before it was reported without a location. Examples: GetIdentifierLocation, GetLocation or GetParameterListLocation returning null, or Location.None. This can hide legitimate analyzer warnings.
The BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull path (a Key attribute with neither an int nor a string value on a metadata member) has no test exercising it.

Problems in a referenced type, such as an unkeyed public member, are now invisible to the consumer. If the defining assembly does not run the analyzer (for example, a third-party NuGet package), the consumer gets no warning while the generated formatter may silently skip or mis-handle that member.

GetPropertyIdentifierLocation casts syntax using 'as PropertyDeclarationSyntax', which returns null for positional record and record-struct properties declared in source (whose DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0].GetSyntax() is ParameterSyntax, e.g. [property: Key(null!)] string Key). Combined with ReportIfLocatedInCompilation at line 1446 dropping any diagnostic whose Location.IsInSource is false, BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull (line 985) is silently suppressed even in the assembly that defines the record.

ReportIfLocatedInCompilation drops all diagnostics where diagnostic.Location.IsInSource is false (Location.None), rather than checking whether the analyzed symbol belongs to this.compilation.Assembly. Roslyn permits analyzers to report Location.None diagnostics; only locations in foreign SyntaxTrees are forbidden. Consequently, any diagnostic on a type in the current compilation whose location helper returns null (for example, GetParameterListLocation at line 1454 when method is null or implicitly declared with empty DeclaringSyntaxReferences) is now silently swallowed.

out_of_scope.description: New documentation section describing a reporting policy for referenced types; not required to fix the crash.
New documentation of the analyzer's scope for referenced types; not required to fix the crash.
The global location filter on reportDiagnostic (lines 239, 1436-1450) changes the reporting of all collector diagnostics, broader than replacing the `[0]` indexing.
